analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy (05 November 2026)
key_insights: The S&P 500 rose 1.58% on 11/4, its best day since August (the report also says best in three months), after Democrats were on course to win both the House and Senate by larger-than-expected margins. Bond yields fell around the world.

Drivers of the rally: relief that the result was not disputed, lower fiscal-trajectory concerns because divided government makes tax cuts and spending packages harder to pass, and lower Treasury yields.

Brent crude fell 8.67% and closed below $100/bbl for the first time since September, easing inflation fears. Part of the move is tied to a reappraisal of the odds of imminent strikes on Iran after the election, and to VP Vance's comment 'The reason we lost is the war'.

Inflation expectations dropped: the Euro 1yr inflation swap fell 25.9bps to a two-month low of 3.10% and the 1yr US inflation swap fell 24.9bps to a two-month low of 2.16%. Investors dialed back the chance of rapid rate hikes.

Treasury yields fell across the curve: 2yr -4.9bps to 4.58%, 10yr -7.6bps to 4.89%, with a further -4.3bps this morning. 10yr bunds fell 5.8bps to 3.27% and 10yr OATs fell 17.6bps to 4.77% (biggest daily decline since April). The Franco-German 10yr spread tightened 11.8bps to 150bps.

The market reaction fits the classic midterm pattern. DB notes that in 20 of 20 midterms since WWII the S&P 500 was higher one year later, and that Republican House losses were on the historical trendline implied by Trump's approval rating.

Large dispersion inside tech: Mag-7 +2.24% (Microsoft +6.68%, Amazon +6.12%, Apple +5.31% to a new all-time high), while CoreWeave fell 9.90% and the Philly semiconductor index fell 3.13%. DB describes a big rotation from data centres to everything else.

Overnight the AI and chip selloff extended on uncertainty over data center regulation after the election: Nasdaq futures -1.18%, KOSPI -5.68% (SK hynix -9.60%, Samsung -7.57%, with a 5 minute trading halt), Nikkei -1.24%. S&P 500 futures are -0.28% and Stoxx futures +0.11%.
Chinese and Australian equities are outperforming: Hang Seng +3.09% after Beijing announced new support measures boosting domestic semiconductor stocks, and the ASX 200 +2.61%.
Trump Media & Technology Group fell 24.54%, its worst day since 2024. The S&P 500 Aerospace & Defense subcomponent fell 1.25%.
European equities rallied: STOXX 600 +1.82% (best day since June), DAX +2.22% (best since April), European banks +4.62% (best since April).

US data was firm: ADP October private payrolls +86k (vs +67k expected) ahead of the jobs report, and ISM services 54.5 (vs 54.8 expected) with prices paid falling to 73.0 from 74.0 prior (74.6 expected).

The Bank of England decides at 12:00 London time and is widely expected to hike 25bp to 4%, its first hike since 2023. DB UK economists expect a 6-3 vote, peak CPI near 4.25% in Q1 2027 and a 2026 growth forecast upgrade to 1.4%.

Euro Area flash October CPI matched consensus with headline at a 3-year high of 4.0% and core at 2.5%. The BOJ's September minutes reinforced the case for further tightening, with one member flagging a possibly faster pace of hikes.
Political fallout: reports say House Speaker Mike Johnson will step down as leader of House Republicans next year, and CBS reported Trump asked advisers whether Defense Secretary Hegseth should go.

risk_factors: Uncertainty over how the election result will affect regulation of data centers, which is pressuring AI and chip stocks.
Nasdaq futures down 1.18% and a 5.68% KOSPI drop point to renewed tech weakness.
The Democratic win was larger than expected, and political fallout is ongoing, including leadership changes in the House Republicans and a possible Hegseth exit.
Inflation risk remains: Euro Area headline CPI is at a 3-year high of 4.0% and the BoE is expected to start hiking.
vol_and_positioning: The Korean index triggered a 5 minute trading halt as KOSPI fell 5.68% overnight.
iTraxx Crossover closed at 306 (-17). iTraxx Europe at 61 (-4), CDX IG at 59 (-3), CDX HY at 106.51 (+0.614 pts).
Fed pricing for further 2026 moves is 21 (+1bp) and ECB pricing is 20 (-3bp), as listed in the key market data.
geopolitical: Reports of a reappraisal of the likelihood of imminent US strikes on Iran after the election, with Defense Secretary Hegseth described as at the hawkish end on the war with Iran.
CBS reported Trump asked advisers whether Hegseth should go.
VP Vance said on X 'The reason we lost is the war', which DB reads as implicitly pointing away from further escalation.
Beijing unveiled fresh support measures that boosted sentiment toward domestic semiconductor companies.
